objective: Seed the local Cloud IaC app module registry from the gate-validated repo-local OpenTofu release-index metadata at startup, while preserving strict nonclaims for registry publish, object-store archive serving, production authentication, deployed endpoints, provider runtime, FD-001 tenant workload hosting, and cloud provisioning.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu discovers services via /.well-known/terraform.json and service identifiers such as modules.v1.
The module registry protocol uses versions and download endpoints below the discovered modules.v1 base path.
Module source addresses are separate from provider credentials, state backends, and plan/apply execution.

implemented_claims: Added OYA_CLOUD_IAC_RELEASE_INDEX_PATH and a default repo-local release-index path to CloudIacAppConfig.

Added a constrained std-only release-index loader that extracts module release rows, rejects empty modules, validates source paths/digests/evidence refs, and rejects credential-like markers before registry publication.
Converted release-index source_path/version pairs into deterministic OpenTofu-compatible git:: source URLs pinned by ref=v<version>.
Changed default app service construction and run_cloud_iac_app to build the module registry from release-index metadata instead of an empty registry.
Updated manifest, catalog, tasks, evidence, and audit-chain scope with truthful local release-index loader claims and nonclaims.
explicit_non_claims: no database adapter or object-store archive serving
no production authentication runtime or Cedar runtime integration
no signed module releases, Sigstore/cosign execution, SLSA, or VSA attestation generation
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no live Argo CD rollout, Kubernetes rollout, or Jenkins pipeline execution
no measured SLO, DR, sharding execution, tenant migration, or capacity telemetry
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant evidence
no aggregate ./bin/oya gate run-all success claim for current worktree
false_green_findings_closed: The previous app entrypoint could serve discovery and health, but its default registry was empty; default app service construction now loads the local release-index metadata into the registry.
Release-index/archive gates existed independently of app startup; app tests now prove versions and download route responses are backed by the current release-index fixture.
No serde/serde_json dependency was added for this loader; parsing remains constrained to the gate-validated local release-index shape and domain validation still owns release semantics.
known_gaps: The download endpoint still returns source metadata; it does not serve archive bytes from object storage or local ZIP files.
Production authentication, persistence, module object storage, signed releases, OpenTofu plan/apply, provider runtime, and live GitOps/Kubernetes rollout evidence remain future work.
FD-001 remains the product delivery goal; this ChangeSet is substrate progress only and does not prove FD-001 tenant workload hosting.
Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required and aggregate gate run-all are not claimed by this Cloud IaC slice.

findings: Kept the slice boring and local: read one gate-validated release-index shape, validate fields, publish existing domain releases, and reuse existing app/router composition.
Moves Cloud IaC from an empty app registry toward a dogfoodable substrate seam while preserving nonclaims for production readiness, provider runtime, and tenant workload hosting.
RED compile failure proved the loader API was absent; GREEN tests assert both positive release-index routing and negative malformed/credential-like input handling.
Operators can override release-index path with OYA_CLOUD_IAC_RELEASE_INDEX_PATH while defaulting to the repo-local foundation release index.
Focused release-index tests, app tests, and app clippy passed before broader final gates.

alternatives_named: Add serde_json to the app crate
Implement a constrained std-only loader for the gate-validated release-index shape
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The constrained loader avoids adding a dependency seam while closing the empty-default-registry false green for current local metadata.
rejected_reasons: Adding serde_json would expand app dependencies and require new seam rationale for a narrow local bootstrap shape.
Leaving the default registry empty would keep versions/download routes unbacked in the app binary.

findings: The loader rejects credential-like markers in source paths and evidence refs. No credentials, provider tokens, tenant data, or production auth claims were added.
Startup parsing is bounded by the local release-index file and current tests cover six modules. No SLO or load claim is made.
Manifest/catalog/task evidence records local scope and nonclaims; no compliance certification or production rollout is claimed.
The app continues to expose the existing OpenTofu discovery, versions, and download route shapes while seeding data from the existing release-index file.
App startup fails closed if the configured release-index file cannot be read or parsed. Health/liveness routes remain unchanged.
